answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies comes mainly from staking with delayed withdrawal. An agent locks collateral that can be slashed, and its reputation and voting weight scale with stake times tenure. A fake army of clones needs real capital per identity, so cost grows linearly while influence stays near zero. Fresh synthetic accounts look like an empty oasis: surface without water. Exit cooldowns block quick capital recycling, making mass identities a marble-hard expense. An attacker pays heavily yet gains nothing, so the scheme dies. Honest agents keep a safe haven and earn proportionally.
